Exclusion Criterion

In this report we define five exclusion criterion. First, exclude participants with a completion time lower than a third of the median value of the Length of Interview [LOI_{subject} < {Mdn(LOI) \over 3}]. Second, exclude participants whose Country group is different than their Residence OR Native Language [(Residence | Native~Language) != Country]. Third, exclude participants who will report a value below 4 (i.e. 1-3) on the “attentional check” question (i.e. “How serious have you been about filling in the survey?”) [attentional~ check < 4]. Fourth, exclude participants who will report a value below 3 (i.e. 1-2) on the “attentional check” question [attentional~ check < 3]. Fifth, exclude countries with a sample size lower than 250 participants [Sample < 250]. In this report we will run the entire analysis protocol for five exclusion criterion.

df_egypt <- df %>% filter(coupon=="free") %>% filter(Country=='Egypt')
convert_farsi_to_arabic <- function(x) {
  if(x=="٠"|x=="۰"){
    return( "0" )
  } else if (x=="۱" | x=="١"){
    return( "1" )
  } else if (x=="۲" | x=="٢"){
    return( "2" )
  } else if (x=="۳"|x=="٣"){
    return( "3" )
  } else if (x=="۴" | x=="٤"){
    return( "4" )
  } else if (x=="۵" | x=="٥"){
    return( "5" )
  } else if (x=="۶"|x=="٦"){
    return( "6" )
  } else if (x=="۷" | x=="٧"){
    return( "7" )
  } else if (x=="۸" | x=="٨"){
    return( "8" )
  } else if (x=="۹" | x=="٩"){
    return( "9" )
  } else if( any(x %in% as.character(0:9) ) ){
    return( x )
  } else {
    warning( paste("Persian number", x, "not found!!!") )
  }
}

convert <- function(x){
  apply(
    str_split(string = x, pattern = "", simplify = T),
    2,
    convert_farsi_to_arabic
  ) %>% paste0(collapse = "")
}

df[df$Country=='Egypt', "Age"] <-  sapply(as.list(df_egypt$Age), convert)


data_table <- rbind(

    mutate(Age=as.numeric(Age)) %>%

    summarise(
      Country="Pooled",

      `Age, median (IQR) (yr)` = str_c(median(Age), " (", quantile(Age,probs = .25), "-", quantile(Age,probs = .75), ")")
    ),

    group_by(Country) %>%

    )

    Language=ifelse(Country=="Canada", "English, French", Language),

    )

Effect Size


In this section we show the effect size of each study for each country. We use log Odd Ratios (OR) to quantify the effect size of binary variables, while we use Standardized Mean Differences (SMD) as a measure of effect size of continuous variables. Each dot correspond to a country. The dots size indicate the inverse of the standard error (e.g. 1/SE). The red horizontal lines indicate the effect size calculated using the results reported in the original papers. For the Drink and Gym study, we could not calculate the effect size of the original papers as information about pooled standard deviation are not reported. To facilitate the interpretation of the results, the variables are coded in such a way that the effect reported in the original papers are positive in all studies.

data_MrAB_theta <- data_MrAB %>% 
  # EXCLUSION: Full Exclusion
  filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove) ) %>% 
  filter( attention_check_grater_than_3 ) %>% 
  # Calculate mean Financial Literacy
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(FinancialLiteracy = mean(FinancialLiteracy)) %>% 
  group_by(subject, scenario_group) %>% 
  mutate(
    resp = case_when(
      (response[scenario=="gain-gain VS gain"]==1) && (response[scenario=="gain-loss VS gain"]==0) ~ 1, 
      (response[scenario=="loss-loss VS loss"]==1) && (response[scenario=="loss-gain VS loss"]==0) ~ 1,
      T ~ 0
    )
  ) %>% 
  group_by(Country, scenario_group) %>% 
  mutate(
    p = mean(resp),
    n = n(),
    p_h0 = 1/9,
    se_theta = sqrt( 1 / (n * p * (1-p)) ), # SE logit
    logit_data =log( p/(1-p) ),
    logit_h0 = log( p_h0/(1-p_h0) ),
    theta = logit_data-logit_h0 # evidence ratio
  ) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  ungroup()
    
data_Game_theta <- data_Game %>%
  # EXCLUSION: Full Exclusion
  filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove) ) %>% 
  filter( attention_check_grater_than_3 ) %>%

  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(FinancialLiteracy = mean(FinancialLiteracy)) %>%

  group_by(buyer, Country) %>%
  mutate(Odds = n[response==1]/n[response==0]) %>%
  group_by(buyer, Country) %>%
  # filter(Country=="Austria", scenario_group=="gain") %>%
  mutate(se_theta = sqrt(sum(1/n))) %>%
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% select(-response) %>%
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(OR = Odds[buyer=="Stranger"]/Odds[buyer=="Friend"],
         theta = log(OR)) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  select(-c(OR, Odds, n)) %>% ungroup() 

data_Drink_theta <- data_Drink %>% 
  # EXCLUSION: Full Exclusion
  filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove) ) %>% 
  filter( attention_check_grater_than_3 ) %>%

  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(FinancialLiteracy = mean(FinancialLiteracy)) %>% 
  # Remove really really extreme outliers
  filter(response<10000 & response>=0) %>% 
  mutate(response=response+1, logResp=log(response)) %>% 
  # Compute effect size as Standardized Mean Difference
  group_by(Country, store) %>% mutate(n=n()) %>%

  mutate(theta=md/sd(logResp)) %>% 
  group_by(Country, store) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  # -- Calculate standard error -- #
  mutate(first = sum(n) / (n[store=="Resort Hotel"]*n[store=="Grocery Store"]),
         second = theta[1]^2/(2*sum(n)),
         se_theta = sqrt(first+second)) %>% 
  select(-c(md, response, first, second, logResp, n)) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% ungroup()

plot_OR <- data_theta %>% filter(family=="binomial") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x, theta)) +
  geom_jitter( aes(size=1/se_theta, color=Country), width = 0.1, alpha=0.7) +
  geom_point(data = data_paper %>% filter(study!="MrAB") %>% mutate(x=x-2), color="firebrick", size=35, shape="-") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype=2) +
  theme_pubr() + theme(legend.position = "right") +
  labs(x=NULL, y=expression(log(OR))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = viridis::viridis_pal()(nCountries)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = viridis::viridis_pal()(nCountries)) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = "prism_offset", limits = c(-1,5.5), breaks = -1:5) + 
  scale_size(range = c(3, 8)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks =1:4, 
                     labels = unique(data_theta$study[data_theta$family=="binomial"]),
                     guide = "prism_offset") + 
  guides(size = "none") + 
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15), legend.position = "none")

plot_ER <- data_theta %>% filter(family=="binomial1") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x, theta)) +
  geom_jitter( aes(size=1/se_theta, color=Country), width = 0.1, alpha=0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype=2) +
  theme_pubr() + theme(legend.position = "right") +
  labs(x=NULL, y=expression(ER)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = viridis::viridis_pal()(nCountries)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = viridis::viridis_pal()(nCountries)) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = "prism_offset", limits = c(-1,3), breaks = -1:5) +
  scale_size(range = c(3, 8)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks =c(1, 1.5, 2), limits = c(0.5, 2.5),
                     labels = c(" ", "MrAB", ""),
                     guide = "prism_offset") + 
  guides(size = "none") + 
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15), legend.position = "none")

data_MrAB_theta <- data_MrAB %>% 
  # EXCLUSION: Full Exclusion
  filter(native_language_is_country_language | Country!=Residence) %>% 
  filter( !loi_lower_than_loiX0_33 ) %>% 
  filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove) ) %>% 
  filter( attention_check_grater_than_3 ) %>% 
  # Calculate mean Financial Literacy
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(FinancialLiteracy = mean(FinancialLiteracy)) %>% 
  group_by(subject, scenario_group) %>% 
  mutate(
    resp = case_when(
      (response[scenario=="gain-gain VS gain"]==1) && (response[scenario=="gain-loss VS gain"]==0) ~ 1, 
      (response[scenario=="loss-loss VS loss"]==1) && (response[scenario=="loss-gain VS loss"]==0) ~ 1,
      T ~ 0
    )
  ) %>% 
  group_by(Country, scenario_group) %>% 
  mutate(
    p = mean(resp),
    n = n(),
    p_h0 = 1/9,
    se_theta = sqrt( 1 / (n * p * (1-p)) ), # SE logit
    logit_data =log( p/(1-p) ),
    logit_h0 = log( p_h0/(1-p_h0) ),
    theta = logit_data-logit_h0 # evidence ratio
  ) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  ungroup()

  filter( !loi_lower_than_loiX0_33 ) %>% 
  filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove) ) %>% 
  filter( attention_check_grater_than_3 ) %>% 
  # Remove really really extreme outliers
  filter(response<10000 & response>=0) %>% 
  mutate(response=response+1, logResp=log(response)) %>% 
  # Compute effect size as Standardized Mean Difference
  group_by(Country, store) %>% mutate(n=n()) %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  # Calculate Mean Difference 
  mutate(md=mean(logResp[store=="Resort Hotel"])-mean(logResp[store=="Grocery Store"])) %>% 
  # Calculate effect size
  mutate(theta=md/sd(logResp)) %>% 
  group_by(Country, store) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  # -- Calculate standard error -- #
  mutate(first = sum(n) / (n[store=="Resort Hotel"]*n[store=="Grocery Store"]),
         second = theta[1]^2/(2*sum(n)),
         se_theta = sqrt(first+second)) %>% 
  select(-c(md, response, first, second, logResp, n)) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% ungroup()

data_Jacket_theta <- data_Jacket %>%
  # EXCLUSION: Exploratory Exclusion
  filter( !loi_lower_than_loiX0_33 ) %>% 
  filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove) ) %>% 
  filter( attention_check_grater_than_3 ) %>% 
  # Calculate ODD RATIO
  group_by(price, response, Country) %>% 
  mutate(n = n()) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  group_by(price, Country) %>% 
  mutate(Odds = n[response==1]/n[response==0]) %>% 
  group_by(price, Country) %>% 
  # filter(Country=="Austria", scenario_group=="gain") %>% 
  mutate(se_theta = sqrt(sum(1/n))) %>%
  group_by(price, Country) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% select(-response) %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(OR = Odds[price=="low"]/Odds[price=="high"],
         theta = log(OR)) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  select(-c(OR, Odds, n)) %>% ungroup()

                     labels = unique(data_theta$study[data_theta$family=="binomial"]),
                     guide = "prism_offset") +

data_MrAB_theta <- data_MrAB %>% 
   # EXCLUSION: Full Exclusion
  filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove_attention_check_grater_than_2) ) %>% 
  filter( attention_check_grater_than_2 ) %>% 
  # Calculate mean Financial Literacy
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(FinancialLiteracy = mean(FinancialLiteracy)) %>% 
  group_by(subject, scenario_group) %>% 
  mutate(
    resp = case_when(
      (response[scenario=="gain-gain VS gain"]==1) && (response[scenario=="gain-loss VS gain"]==0) ~ 1, 
      (response[scenario=="loss-loss VS loss"]==1) && (response[scenario=="loss-gain VS loss"]==0) ~ 1,
      T ~ 0
    )
  ) %>% 
  group_by(Country, scenario_group) %>% 
  mutate(
    p = mean(resp),
    n = n(),
    p_h0 = 1/9,
    se_theta = sqrt( 1 / (n * p * (1-p)) ), # SE logit
    logit_data =log( p/(1-p) ),
    logit_h0 = log( p_h0/(1-p_h0) ),
    theta = logit_data-logit_h0 # evidence ratio
  ) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  ungroup()

  # filter(Country=="Austria", scenario_group=="gain") %>% 
  mutate(se_theta = sqrt(sum(1/n))) %>%
  group_by(loss, Country) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% select(-response) %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(OR = Odds[loss=="cash"]/Odds[loss=="ticket"],
         theta = log(OR)) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  select(-c(OR, Odds, n)) %>% ungroup()

data_Gym_theta <- data_Gym %>%
  # EXCLUSION: Full Exclusion
  filter( T ) %>% 
  # Calculate Mean Difference
  group_by(frame, Country) %>% mutate(n = n()) %>%
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(pooled_sd = sd(response),
         md = mean(response[frame=="Yearly"])-mean(response[frame=="Per-session"]),
         theta = md/pooled_sd) %>% 
  group_by(frame, Country) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>%
  # -- Calculate standard error -- #
  mutate(first = sum(n) / (n[frame=="Per-session"]*n[frame=="Yearly"]),
         second = theta[1]^2/(2*sum(n)),
         se_theta = sqrt(first+second)) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% ungroup() %>% 
  select(-c(md, first, second, pooled_sd, n, response))

data_Plane_theta <- data_Plane %>%
  # EXCLUSION: No Exclusion
  filter( T ) %>% 
  # Calculate ODD RATIO
  group_by(coupon, response, Country) %>% 
  mutate(n = n()) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  group_by(coupon, Country) %>% 
  mutate(Odds = n[response==1]/n[response==0]) %>% 
  group_by(coupon, Country) %>% 
  # filter(Country=="Austria", scenario_group=="gain") %>% 
  mutate(se_theta = sqrt(sum(1/n))) %>%
  group_by(coupon, Country) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% select(-response) %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(OR = Odds[coupon=="purchased"]/Odds[coupon=="free"],
         theta = log(OR)) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  select(-c(OR, Odds, n)) %>% ungroup()

theta_noExclusion <- list(
  MrAB = data_MrAB_theta %>% 
    mutate(study="MrAB", x=ifelse(scenario_group=="gain", 1, 2),
           family="binomial1") %>% 
    select(-c(X, scenario)) %>% rename(condition = scenario_group),
  Game = data_Game_theta %>% mutate(study="Game", x=1, family="binomial") %>% 
    select(-c(X, market_value)) %>% rename(condition = buyer),
  Drink = data_Drink_theta %>% mutate(study="Drink", x=1, family="gaussian") %>% 
    select(-c(X)) %>% rename(condition = store),
  Jacket = data_Jacket_theta %>% mutate(study="Jacket", x=2, family="binomial") %>% 
    select(-c(X)) %>% rename(condition = price),
  Play = data_Play_theta %>% mutate(study="Play", x=3, family="binomial") %>% 
    select(-c(X)) %>% rename(condition = loss),
  Gym = data_Gym_theta %>% mutate(study="Gym", x=2, family="gaussian") %>% 
    select(-c(X)) %>% rename(condition = frame),
  Plane = data_Plane_theta %>% mutate(study="Plane", x=4, family="binomial") %>% 
    select(-c(X)) %>% rename(condition = coupon)
)

Bayesian Meta-Analysis


In this section we perform a Bayesian meta-analysis. The purple dots indicate the population level estimates, while the gray dots indicate the estimates of each country. Our results show that the population effect replicate the original findings for each study, regardless of the exclusion criterion used.

  • Full

Compute Bayes Factor 
# re-run1 
compute_bayes_factor <- function(model){
  intercept <- as_draws(model, variable = "b_Intercept")
  posterior <- as.vector(unlist(intercept))
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(posterior),mean=0,sd=1)
  bayesfactor_parameters(posterior,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
}

Within- vs Between-Subjects Comparison

For the Jacket, Play, and Plane scenarios (between-subjects in the original studies), we probe whether our within-subjects design affected the estimates in two ways: (i) a between-subjects test based on the first condition each participant encountered, and (ii) a robustness check using a single, randomly selected condition per participant.

First condition presented (between subjects)

The raw Qualtrics exports record the order in which the four scenario blocks were presented. The two conditions of each of these scenarios were always placed in different blocks, so the recorded block order identifies which condition each participant encountered first. Keeping only the response to the first-encountered condition yields a between-subjects design with random assignment, free from carryover from the other condition. The code below reconstructs the presentation order, fits the between-subjects pooled model on the first-encountered responses, and reports the 95% credible interval of the difference (within − between).

Block presentation order from the raw Qualtrics exports 
# Position (1-4) at which each scenario block was shown to each participant.
# Block contents (confirmed against the QSF):
#   block 1 (FL_14): MrAB1, Game1, Drink1, Gym1, Jacket1
#   block 2 (FL_15): Game2, MrAB2, Play2, Plane2
#   block 3 (FL_16): MrAB3, Game3, Jacket2, Gym2
#   block 4 (FL_17): MrAB4, Play1, Plane1, Drink2
block_order <- map_dfr(
  list.files("../Data/raw", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE),
  function(f){
    dat <- suppressWarnings(read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE))
    dat <- dat[3:nrow(dat), ] # drop question text and ImportId rows
    do_cols <- sort(grep("FL_5_DO_FL_1[4-7]", names(dat), value = TRUE))
    out <- dat[, do_cols]
    names(out) <- c("pos_block1", "pos_block2", "pos_block3", "pos_block4")
    out$subject <- dat$ResponseId
    out
  }) %>%
  filter(if_all(starts_with("pos_"), ~ . != "")) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("pos_"), as.numeric)) %>%
  as_tibble()
First-condition (between-subjects) computation 
between_first_condition <- function(data, condition_col, conditions,
                                    condition_blocks, m_within, original) {

  # Keep, for each participant, only the condition they encountered first
  data_first <- data %>%
    mutate(condition = .data[[condition_col]]) %>%
    filter(!(Country %in% countries2remove), attention_check_grater_than_3) %>%
    dplyr::select(Country, subject, condition, response) %>% as_tibble() %>%
    inner_join(block_order, by = "subject") %>%
    mutate(first_condition = ifelse(
      .data[[condition_blocks[1]]] < .data[[condition_blocks[2]]],
      conditions[1], conditions[2])) %>%
    filter(condition == first_condition)

  # Per-country log odds-ratio (theta) and its standard error
  databetween_theta <- data_first %>%
    group_by(Country) %>%
    summarise(
      n1 = sum(response == 1 & condition == conditions[1]),
      n0 = sum(response == 0 & condition == conditions[1]),
      m1 = sum(response == 1 & condition == conditions[2]),
      m0 = sum(response == 0 & condition == conditions[2]),
      theta    = log((n1 / n0) / (m1 / m0)),
      se_theta = sqrt(1 / n1 + 1 / n0 + 1 / m1 + 1 / m0),
      .groups = "drop")

  # Between-subjects pooled effect (aggregated theta per country)
  m_between <- brm(theta | se(se_theta) ~ 1 + (1 | Country),
                   prior = prior_string("normal(0,2.5)", class = "Intercept"),
                   data = databetween_theta, iter = 20000, seed = 123, refresh = 0)

  # Pooled-effect posterior, within vs between, and CI of their difference
  within_samples  <- as.numeric(prepare_predictions(m_within)$dpars$mu$fe$b)
  between_samples <- as.numeric(prepare_predictions(m_between)$dpars$mu$fe$b)
  ci <- quantile(within_samples - between_samples, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

  df <- rbind(data.frame(post = between_samples, type = "between"),
              data.frame(post = within_samples,  type = "within"))
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(post, color = type, fill = type)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = original, color = "#472E7CFF", linewidth = 2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("#FFC857", "#2A9D8F")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#FFC857", "#2A9D8F")) +
    theme_pubr() +
    theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 16), title = element_text(size = 20)) +
    labs(y = "Density", x = "Posterior log(Odd-Ratio)", color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 2.5))

  list(n = nrow(data_first), estimate = fixef(m_between), ci = ci, plot = p)
}

                                        c("pos_block1", "pos_block3"), mJacket, original_theta$Jacket$theta)
play_first   <- between_first_condition(data_Play,   "loss",   c("cash", "ticket"),
                                        c("pos_block2", "pos_block4"), mPlay,   original_theta$Play$theta)
plane_first  <- between_first_condition(data_Plane,  "coupon", c("purchased", "free"),

Random single response (robustness check)

We additionally re-estimate each effect using a single, randomly selected condition per participant and compare it with the within-subjects estimate. The code below builds the random split, fits the between-subjects pooled model, and reports the 95% credible interval of the difference (within − between).

Within- vs between-subjects computation 
between_vs_within <- function(data, condition_col, conditions, m_within, original) {

  # Assign each participant to a single (between-subjects) condition
  data_random <- data %>%
    mutate(condition = .data[[condition_col]]) %>%
    filter(!(Country %in% countries2remove), attention_check_grater_than_3) %>%
    select(Country, subject, condition, response) %>% as_tibble() %>%
    group_by(Country, condition) %>% mutate(sbjtype = row_number() %% 2) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(sbjtype = ifelse(condition == conditions[1], sbjtype, 1 - sbjtype)) %>%
    filter(as.logical(sbjtype)) %>% select(-sbjtype)

  # Per-country log odds-ratio (theta) and its standard error
  databetween_theta <- data_random %>%
    group_by(condition, response, Country) %>% mutate(n = n()) %>% filter(row_number() == 1) %>%
    group_by(condition, Country) %>% mutate(Odds = n[response == 1] / n[response == 0]) %>%
    mutate(se_theta = sqrt(sum(1 / n))) %>% filter(row_number() == 1) %>% select(-response) %>%
    group_by(Country) %>%
    mutate(OR = Odds[condition == conditions[1]] / Odds[condition == conditions[2]],
           theta = log(OR)) %>%
    filter(row_number() == 1) %>% select(-c(OR, Odds, n, condition)) %>% ungroup()

  # Between-subjects pooled effect (fast: aggregated theta per country)
  m_between <- brm(theta | se(se_theta) ~ 1 + (1 | Country),
                   prior = prior_string("normal(0,2.5)", class = "Intercept"),
                   data = databetween_theta, iter = 20000, seed = 123, refresh = 0)

  # Pooled-effect posterior, within vs between, and CI of their difference
  within_samples  <- as.numeric(prepare_predictions(m_within)$dpars$mu$fe$b)
  between_samples <- as.numeric(prepare_predictions(m_between)$dpars$mu$fe$b)
  ci <- quantile(within_samples - between_samples, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

  df <- rbind(data.frame(post = between_samples, type = "between"),
              data.frame(post = within_samples,  type = "within"))
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(post, color = type, fill = type)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = original, color = "#472E7CFF", linewidth = 2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("#FFC857", "#2A9D8F")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#FFC857", "#2A9D8F")) +
    theme_pubr() +
    theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 16), title = element_text(size = 20)) +
    labs(y = "Density", x = "Posterior log(Odd-Ratio)", color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 2.5))

  list(ci = ci, plot = p)
}

Compute Bayes Factor 
# re-run1
compute_bayes_factor <- function(model){
  intercept <- as_draws(model, variable = "b_Intercept")
  posterior <- as.vector(unlist(intercept))
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(posterior),mean=0,sd=1)
  bayesfactor_parameters(posterior,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
}


log10_bf <- c(
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mMrAB1))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mMrAB2))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mGame))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mDrink))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mJacket))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mPlay))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mGym))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mPlane))), 2)
)

Compute Bayes Factor 
# re-run
compute_bayes_factor <- function(model){
  intercept <- as_draws(model, variable = "b_Intercept")
  posterior <- as.vector(unlist(intercept))
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(posterior),mean=0,sd=1)
  bayesfactor_parameters(posterior,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
}

log10_bf <- c(
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mMrAB1))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mMrAB2))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mGame))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mDrink))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mJacket))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mPlay))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mGym))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mPlane))), 2)
)

Compute Bayes Factor 
# re-run
compute_bayes_factor <- function(model){
  intercept <- as_draws(model, variable = "b_Intercept")
  posterior <- as.vector(unlist(intercept))
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(posterior),mean=0,sd=1)
  bayesfactor_parameters(posterior,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
}

log10_bf <- c(
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mMrAB1))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mMrAB2))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mGame))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mDrink))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mJacket))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mPlay))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mGym))), 2),
  round(log10(as.numeric(compute_bayes_factor(mPlane))), 2)
)

Unpooled Analysis


In this section we perform a Bayesian unpooled analysis. We will compute the effect size for each scenario and country independently. We will then compare each of them with the effect sizes found in the original papers.

  • Partial
  • Full

ph0 <- 1/9
logit_h0 <- log(ph0 / (1-ph0))

mMrAB1 <- brm(response ~ 0 + Country,
              prior = prior_string( str_c("normal(",logit_h0,",2.5)"), class = "b"),
              data = data_MrAB %>% 
                # EXCLUSION: Full Exclusion
                filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove) ) %>% 
                filter( attention_check_grater_than_3 ) %>% 
                filter(scenario_group=="gain") %>% 
                group_by(subject) %>% 
                mutate(
                  response = ifelse(
                    (response[scenario=="gain-gain VS gain"]==1) && (response[scenario=="gain-loss VS gain"]==0), 1, 0
                  )
                ) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% ungroup(), 
              iter = 20000, refresh = 0, family="bernoulli", cores = 4)


mMrAB2 <- brm(response ~ 0 + Country,
              prior = prior_string( str_c("normal(",logit_h0,",2.5)"), class = "b"),
              data = data_MrAB %>% 
                # EXCLUSION: Full Exclusion
                filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove) ) %>% 
                filter( attention_check_grater_than_3 ) %>% 
                filter(scenario_group=="loss") %>% 
                group_by(subject) %>% 
                mutate(
                  response = as.integer(response[scenario=="loss-loss VS loss"]==1 && response[scenario=="loss-gain VS loss"]==0)
                  ) %>% 
                filter(row_number()==1) %>% ungroup(),
              iter = 20000, refresh = 0, family="bernoulli", cores = 4)

for( country in unique(post_plot1$Country) ){

}

                       .[,"study",drop=T] %>% unique(),
                     guide = "prism_offset") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#228B8DFF", "gray"), breaks = c("yes", "no")) +
  guides(size = "none") + 
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15, family="Arial"), legend.position = "none")

plotER <- post %>% filter(family=="binomial1") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x, theta, color=credible)) +
  geom_jitter( width = 0.1, alpha=0.7, size=4 ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype=2, size=1) +
  theme_pubr() + theme(legend.position = "right") +
  labs(x=NULL, y="Posterior Evidence Ratio") +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = "prism_offset", limits = c(-1,3), breaks = -1:5) +
  scale_size(range = c(3, 8)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks =c(1, 1.5, 2), limits = c(0.5, 2.5),
                     labels = c(" ", "MrAB", ""),
                     guide = "prism_offset") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#228B8DFF", "gray"), breaks = c("yes", "no")) +
  guides(size = "none") + 
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15, family="Arial"), legend.position = "none")

plotSMD <- post %>% filter(family=="gaussian") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x, theta, color=credible)) +
  geom_jitter( width = 0.1, alpha=0.7, size=4 ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype=2, size=1) +
  theme_pubr() + theme(legend.position = "right") +
  labs(x=NULL, y="Posterior Standardized\nMean Difference") +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = "prism_offset", limits = c(-1,3), breaks = -1:5) +
  scale_size(range = c(3, 8)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:2, limits = c(0.5, 2.5),
                     labels = post %>% filter(family=="gaussian") %>% 
                       .[,"study",drop=T] %>% unique(),
                     guide = "prism_offset") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#228B8DFF", "gray"), breaks = c("yes", "no")) +
  guides(size = "none") + 
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15, family="Arial"), legend.position = "none")

              prior = prior_string( str_c("normal(",logit_h0,",2.5)"), class = "b"),
              data = data_MrAB %>% 
                filter(scenario_group=="gain") %>% 
                # EXCLUSION: Full Exclusion
                filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove) ) %>% 
                filter( attention_check_grater_than_2 ) %>% 
                group_by(subject) %>% 
                mutate(
                  response = ifelse(
                    (response[scenario=="gain-gain VS gain"]==1) && (response[scenario=="gain-loss VS gain"]==0), 1, 0
                  )
                ) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% ungroup(), 
              iter = 5000, refresh = 0, family="bernoulli", cores = 4)

              data = data_MrAB %>%

                # EXCLUSION: Full Exclusion
                filter( !(Country %in% countries2remove) ) %>%

# re-run
post_plot1$log10_bf = NA
for( country in unique(post_plot1$Country) ){
  idx = post_plot1$Country==country
  beta <- post_plot1$theta[idx]
  posterior <- as.vector(unlist(beta))
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(posterior),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf <- bayesfactor_parameters(posterior,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  post_plot1$log10_bf[idx] <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf)), 2)
}

  rename(Estimate = mu) %>% 
  mutate(` ` = "") %>%

# re-run
post_plot1$log10_bf = NA
for( country in unique(post_plot1$Country) ){
  idx = post_plot1$Country==country
  beta <- post_plot1$theta[idx]
  posterior <- as.vector(unlist(beta))
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(posterior),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf <- bayesfactor_parameters(posterior,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  post_plot1$log10_bf[idx] <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf)), 2)
}

                       .[,"study",drop=T] %>% unique(),
                     guide = "prism_offset") +

  guides(size = "none") +

    data.frame(theta, Country=country, study="MrAB", family="binomial1", x=1) %>% 
      mutate(lower = HDInterval::hdi( theta )["lower"],
             upper = HDInterval::hdi( theta )["upper"],
             credible = ifelse(lower<0, "no", "yes"))
})

  mutate(theta=mean(theta)) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1)

# re-run
post_plot1$log10_bf = NA
for( country in unique(post_plot1$Country) ){
  idx = post_plot1$Country==country
  beta <- post_plot1$theta[idx]
  posterior <- as.vector(unlist(beta))
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(posterior),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf <- bayesfactor_parameters(posterior,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  post_plot1$log10_bf[idx] <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf)), 2)
}

table_unpooled <- post_plot1 %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% mutate(mu=mean(theta)) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  select(Country, mu, lower, upper, log10_bf) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(`CIs (95%)`=str_c(round(lower,2), round(upper,2), sep = ' - '),
         mu=round(mu,2)) %>% 
  rename(Estimate = mu) %>% 
  mutate(` ` = "") %>% 
  .[,c(7,1,2, 6,5)]

mMrAB1 <- brm(response ~ 0 + Country,
              prior = prior_string( str_c("normal(",logit_h0,",2.5)"), class = "b"),
              data = data_MrAB %>% 
                filter(scenario_group=="gain") %>% 
                group_by(subject) %>% 
                mutate(
                  response = ifelse(
                    (response[scenario=="gain-gain VS gain"]==1) && (response[scenario=="gain-loss VS gain"]==0), 1, 0
                  )
                ) %>% filter(row_number()==1) %>% ungroup(), 
              iter = 5000, refresh = 0, family="bernoulli")


mMrAB2 <- brm(response ~ 0 + Country,
              prior = prior_string( str_c("normal(",logit_h0,",2.5)"), class = "b"),
              data = data_MrAB %>%
                filter(scenario_group=="loss") %>% 
                group_by(subject) %>% 
                mutate(
                  response = as.integer(response[scenario=="loss-loss VS loss"]==1 && response[scenario=="loss-gain VS loss"]==0)
                  ) %>% 
                filter(row_number()==1) %>% ungroup(),
              iter = 5000, refresh = 0, family="bernoulli")

# re-run
post <- prepare_predictions(mMrAB1)$dpars$mu$fe$b %>% 
  as.data.frame()

names(post)[1] <- "Austria"
names(post) <- str_remove( names(post), "b_Country" )
all_countries <- names(post)

post_plot1 <- map_dfr(all_countries, function(country){
    theta <- post[,country] - logit_h0
    
    data.frame(theta, Country=country, study="MrAB", family="binomial1", x=1) %>% 
      mutate(lower = HDInterval::hdi( theta )["lower"],
             upper = HDInterval::hdi( theta )["upper"],
             credible = ifelse(lower<0, "no", "yes"))
})

postMrAB1 <- post_plot1 %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(theta=mean(theta)) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1)

plMrAB1 <- post_plot1 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = theta, y = Country)) +
  stat_halfeye(aes(fill=credible, color=credible)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype=2) +
  theme_pubr() + 
  labs(x="Posterior Evidence Ratio", y=NULL) +
  scale_y_discrete(guide = "prism_offset") + 
  scale_x_continuous(guide = "prism_offset") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#228B8DFF", "gray"), breaks = c("yes", "no")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#33628DFF", "gray"), breaks = c("yes", "no")) +
  guides(size = "none") + 
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15),
        legend.position = "none")

# re-run
post_plot1$log10_bf = NA
for( country in unique(post_plot1$Country) ){
  idx = post_plot1$Country==country
  beta <- post_plot1$theta[idx]
  posterior <- as.vector(unlist(beta))
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(posterior),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf <- bayesfactor_parameters(posterior,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  post_plot1$log10_bf[idx] <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf)), 2)
}

table_unpooled <- post_plot1 %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% mutate(mu=mean(theta)) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  select(Country, mu, lower, upper, log10_bf) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(`CIs (95%)`=str_c(round(lower,2), round(upper,2), sep = ' - '),
         mu=round(mu,2)) %>% 
  rename(Estimate = mu) %>% 
  mutate(` ` = "") %>% 
  .[,c(7,1,2, 6,5)]

  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype=2) +
  theme_pubr() + 
  labs(x=expression(SMD), y=NULL) +
  scale_y_discrete(guide = "prism_offset") + 
  scale_x_continuous(guide = "prism_offset") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#228B8DFF", "gray"), breaks = c("yes", "no")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#33628DFF", "gray"), breaks = c("yes", "no")) +
  guides(size = "none") + 
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15),
        legend.position = "none")

             data = data_Plane,
             iter = 5000, refresh = 0, family="bernoulli")
Plot posteriors 
post <- prepare_predictions(mPlane)$dpars$mu$fe$b %>% 
  as.data.frame()

names(post)[1] <- "Austria"
names(post)[2] <- "theta"
names(post) <- str_remove( names(post), "b_" )
names(post) <- str_remove( names(post), "coupon" )
names(post) <- str_remove( names(post), "Country" )
all_countries <- names(post)[-2]
all_countries <- all_countries[-grep(":", all_countries)]

post_plot <- map_dfr(all_countries, function(country){
  if(country=="Austria"){
    theta <- post[,"theta"]
  } else {
    theta <- post[,"theta"] + post[,grep(paste0(":",country), names(post))]
  }
  data.frame(theta, Country=country, study="Plane", family="binomial", x=4) %>% 
    mutate(lower = HDInterval::hdi( theta )["lower"],
           upper = HDInterval::hdi( theta )["upper"],
           credible = ifelse(lower<0, "no", "yes"))
})

postPlane <- post_plot %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  mutate(theta=mean(theta)) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1)

# Get Country-level Info
zscore <- function(x) as.vector(scale(x))
info <- 
  read.csv("../Data/Info Countries/data.csv") %>% 
  filter(Country %in% unique(post$Country)) %>% 
  select(Country, GDP.per.capita..current.US.., GINI.index, Democracy.index) %>%
  rename(
    GDPxCapita = GDP.per.capita..current.US..,
    Gini = GINI.index,
    democracy_index=Democracy.index
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # GDPxCapita: Remove (2022) and convert in number
    GDPxCapita = str_replace(GDPxCapita, "\\([^()]{0,}\\)", ""),
    GDPxCapita = str_remove(GDPxCapita, ","),
    GDPxCapita = as.numeric(GDPxCapita),
    # Gini: Remove (2022), remove comma, convert to number, scale to 0-1
    Gini = str_replace(Gini, "\\([^()]{0,}\\)", ""),
    Gini = str_remove(Gini, ","),
    Gini = as.numeric(Gini) / 100,
    democracy_index = str_replace(democracy_index, ",", "."),
    democracy_index=as.numeric(democracy_index)
  )

# Create a named vector for all countries
currency_codes <- c(
    "Austria" = "EUR",      # Euro

    "Canada" = "CAD",       # Canadian Dollar
    "China" = "CNY",        # Chinese Yuan
    "Denmark" = "DKK",      # Danish Krone
    "Egypt" = "EGP",        # Egyptian Pound
    "France" = "EUR",       # Euro
    "Germany" = "EUR",      # Euro
    "India" = "INR",        # Indian Rupee
    "Indonesia" = "IDR",    # Indonesian Rupiah
    "Italy" = "EUR",        # Euro
    "Lithuania" = "EUR",    # Euro
    "Morocco" = "MAD",      # Moroccan Dirham
    "Netherlands" = "EUR",  # Euro
    "Portugal" = "EUR",     # Euro
    "Romania" = "RON",      # Romanian Leu
    "Spain" = "EUR",        # Euro
    "Sweden" = "SEK",       # Swedish Krona
    "Switzerland" = "CHF",  # Swiss Franc
    "USA" = "USD",          # US Dollar
    "Vietnam" = "VND"       # Vietnamese Dong
)

# Create results dataframe and merge with exchange rates
exchange_rate_df <- data.frame(
    Country = names(currency_codes),
    Currency = currency_codes
) %>%
    left_join(exchange_rates, by = "Currency")

theta <- map_dfr(theta_preregisteredExclusion, function(df) df )

sbj_regressors <- Gym %>% 
  # Tidy
  mutate(Age=as.numeric(Age)) %>%
  filter(Age>0 & Age<99) %>% 
  mutate(Education=as.numeric(Education)) %>% 
  filter(Education<100) %>% 
  filter(Gender%in%c("Male", "Female")) %>% 
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  summarise(FinancialLiteracy=mean(FinancialLiteracy),
            numeric_income=mean(numeric_income, na.rm=T),
            Education=mean(Education),
            Age=mean(Age))

lor2smd = sqrt( 3 / (pi^2) )
df <- left_join(theta[,c("Country", "theta", "se_theta", "family", "study", "x")], info, by="Country") %>% 
  mutate(study = ifelse(family=="binomial1" & x==1, "MrAB1", study),
         study = ifelse(family=="binomial1" & x==2, "MrAB2", study)) %>% 
  left_join(sbj_regressors, by="Country") %>% 
  group_by(study) %>% 
  mutate( zGDPxCapita=zscore(GDPxCapita) ) %>% 
  mutate( choensd = ifelse(family=="binomial", theta*lor2smd, theta),
          choensd = ifelse(family=="binomial1", NA, choensd) ) %>% 
  mutate( se = ifelse(family=="binomial", se_theta*lor2smd, se_theta),
          se = ifelse(family=="binomial1", NA, se) ) %>% 
  left_join(exchange_rate_df, by="Country")
Fit Linear Model 
# All ---------------------
fit_and_save_mAll_Others <- function(){
  path2file <- "scr/country-level-analysis/models/Others/mAll.rds"
  
  if( file.exists(path2file) ){
    m <- readRDS(file = path2file)
  } else {
    m <- brm(
      formula = choensd ~ zGDPxCapita + zFinancialLiteracy + zEducation + zAge + zIncome + (zGDPxCapita + zFinancialLiteracy + zEducation + zAge + zIncome | study), 
      prior = prior_string("normal(0,2.5)", class = "b"),
      data = df %>% group_by(study) %>% 
        mutate(
          zFinancialLiteracy=zscore(FinancialLiteracy),
          zEducation=zscore(Education),
          zAge=zscore(Age),
          zIncome=zscore(numeric_income)
        ),
      iter = 20000, refresh = 100, cores = 4
    )
    saveRDS(m, file = path2file)
  }
  return(m)
}
mAll <- fit_and_save_mAll_Others()
Fit Non-Linear Model 
d <- df %>% mutate(x=zscore(GDPxCapita), y=choensd) %>% filter(family!="binomial1")
fit_and_save_nlbmGDPxCapita <- function(){
  path2file <- "scr/country-level-analysis/models/Others/nlbmGDPxCapita.rds"
  
  if( file.exists(path2file) ){
    m <- readRDS(file = path2file)
  } else {
    
    # Define the nonlinear formula with random effects
    nlform <- bf(
      y ~ K / (1 + exp(-r * (x - x0))),
      K ~ 1 + (1 | study), # Random effect for K
      r ~ 1 + (1 | study), # Random effect for r
      x0 ~ 1 + (1 | study), # Random effect for x0
      nl = TRUE
    )
    
    # Define priors (adjust these based on your knowledge)
    priors <- c(
      prior(normal(1, 1), nlpar = "K"),
      prior(normal(0, 2.5), nlpar = "r"),
      prior(normal(-1, 1), nlpar = "x0")
    )
    
    # Fit the model
    m <- brm(
      formula = nlform,
      data = d,
      prior = priors,
      family = gaussian(),
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
      chains = 4,
      iter = 20000,
      cores = 4,
      seed = 123
    )
    
    saveRDS(m, file = path2file)
  }
  
  return(m)
}
bm1 <- fit_and_save_nlbmGDPxCapita()
Plot 
# Figure 2 - Individual Differences + GDP
# Mirrors scr/country-level-analysis/figure-2.R so the report and the article
# figure share the same plotting style.
#   Panel A: Financial Literacy | Education | Age | Income
#            (per-scenario credible intervals + Overall posterior).
#   Panel B: GDP growth rate ridge + GDP logistic curve + flag legend.
library(ggflags)
nlgdp <- bm1  # non-linear GDP model (named bm1 earlier in this report)

# Configuration ------------------------------------------------------------
linear_preds <- c("zFinancialLiteracy", "zEducation", "zAge", "zIncome")
predictor_labels <- c(
  zFinancialLiteracy = "Financial Literacy",
  zEducation = "Education",
  zAge = "Age",
  zIncome = "Income",
  gdp = "GDP per Capita"
)
predictor_colors <- c(
  zFinancialLiteracy = "#B07AA1",
  zEducation = "#F28E2B",
  zAge = "#59A14F",
  zIncome = "#E15759",
  gdp = "#4E79A7"
)

study_names <- rownames(ranef(mAll)$study[, , 1])
x_levels <- c(" ", study_names, " ", "Overall")

# Extract posteriors: linear predictors ------------------------------------
draws <- as_draws_df(mAll)
study_posteriors_lin <- map_dfr(linear_preds, function(pred) {
  fe_col <- paste0("b_", pred)
  map_dfr(study_names, function(s) {
    re_col <- paste0("r_study[", s, ",", pred, "]")
    tibble(estimate = draws[[fe_col]] + draws[[re_col]], study = s, predictor = pred)
  })
})
fe_posteriors_lin <- map_dfr(linear_preds, function(pred) {
  fe_col <- paste0("b_", pred)
  tibble(estimate = draws[[fe_col]], study = "Overall", predictor = pred)
})

# Extract posteriors: GDP growth rate (r) ----------------------------------
draws_gdp <- as_draws_df(nlgdp)
study_posteriors_gdp <- map_dfr(study_names, function(s) {
  re_col <- paste0("r_study__r[", s, ",Intercept]")
  tibble(estimate = draws_gdp[["b_r_Intercept"]] + draws_gdp[[re_col]], study = s, predictor = "gdp")
})
fe_posteriors_gdp <- tibble(estimate = draws_gdp[["b_r_Intercept"]], study = "Overall", predictor = "gdp")

# Combine posteriors -------------------------------------------------------
study_posteriors <- bind_rows(study_posteriors_lin, study_posteriors_gdp)
fe_posteriors <- bind_rows(fe_posteriors_lin, fe_posteriors_gdp)
study_posteriors$study <- factor(study_posteriors$study, levels = x_levels)
fe_posteriors$study <- factor(fe_posteriors$study, levels = x_levels)

# Pre-compute intervals ----------------------------------------------------
intervals <- study_posteriors %>%
  group_by(study, predictor) %>%
  summarise(
    q025 = quantile(estimate, 0.025),
    q10  = quantile(estimate, 0.10),
    q25  = quantile(estimate, 0.25),
    med  = median(estimate),
    q75  = quantile(estimate, 0.75),
    q90  = quantile(estimate, 0.90),
    q975 = quantile(estimate, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Helper: make interval panel ----------------------------------------------
make_panel <- function(pred_name, show_y = TRUE, show_x = TRUE,
                       ylimits = NULL, flip = FALSE,
                       show_zero_line = TRUE) {
  int_data <- intervals %>% filter(predictor == pred_name)
  fe_data <- fe_posteriors %>% filter(predictor == pred_name)
  clr <- predictor_colors[[pred_name]]

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_linerange(data = int_data, aes(x = study, ymin = q025, ymax = q975),
                   color = clr, linewidth = 2, alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_linerange(data = int_data, aes(x = study, ymin = q10, ymax = q90),
                   color = clr, linewidth = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_linerange(data = int_data, aes(x = study, ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
                   color = clr, linewidth = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = int_data, aes(x = study, y = med), color = clr, size = 1.5) +
    stat_halfeye(data = fe_data, aes(x = study, y = estimate),
                 fill = clr, color = clr, alpha = 0.5,
                 .width = 0.95, slab_color = NA, point_size = 2.5,
                 adjust = 0.5, width = 0.6) +
    {if (show_zero_line) geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray")} +
    ggtitle(predictor_labels[[pred_name]]) +
    theme_pubr() +
    theme(
      text = element_text(size = 15, family = "Arial"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 13)
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(guide = "prism_offset") +
    scale_x_discrete(breaks = c(study_names, "Overall"), guide = "prism_offset", drop = FALSE)

  if (show_y) {
    if (pred_name == "gdp") {
      p <- p + labs(y = "Growth Rate")
    } else {
      p <- p + labs(y = "Beta Estimate")
    }
  } else {
    p <- p + labs(y = NULL)
  }

  if (flip && !is.null(ylimits)) {
    p <- p + coord_flip(ylim = ylimits)
  } else if (flip) {
    p <- p + coord_flip()
  } else if (!is.null(ylimits)) {
    p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylimits)
  }

  if (!show_x) {
    if (flip) {
      p <- p + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.line.y = element_blank())
    } else {
      p <- p + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
    }
  }

  return(p)
}

# Create interval panels ---------------------------------------------------
ylim_linear <- c(-0.22, 0.22)
p_fl  <- make_panel("zFinancialLiteracy", show_y = FALSE, show_x = TRUE,  ylimits = ylim_linear, flip = TRUE)
p_edu <- make_panel("zEducation",         show_y = FALSE, show_x = FALSE, ylimits = ylim_linear, flip = TRUE)
p_age <- make_panel("zAge",               show_y = FALSE, show_x = FALSE, ylimits = ylim_linear, flip = TRUE)
p_inc <- make_panel("zIncome",            show_y = FALSE, show_x = FALSE, ylimits = ylim_linear, flip = TRUE)
p_gdp <- make_panel("gdp",                show_y = FALSE, ylimits = NULL, flip = TRUE)

# GDP curve (Figure 2B) ----------------------------------------------------
f <- function(x, K, r, x0) K / (1 + exp(-r * (x - x0)))
d <- df %>% filter(family != "binomial1") %>% mutate(x = zscore(GDPxCapita), y = choensd)

p_curve <- df %>%
  filter(family != "binomial1") %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  mutate(choensd = mean(choensd)) %>%
  filter(row_number() == 1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(GDPxCapita, choensd)) +
  geom_line(
    data = data.frame(
      GDPxCapita = seq(-2, 100, .01) * 1000,
      choensd = f(seq(-2, 100, .01) * 1000, fixef(nlgdp)[1, 1],
                  fixef(nlgdp)[2, 1] / sd(d$GDPxCapita),
                  fixef(nlgdp)[3, 1] * sd(d$GDPxCapita) + mean(d$GDPxCapita))
    ),
    linewidth = 2, color = "#5f7e96"
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 10, shape = 1) +
  geom_flag(aes(country = flag), size = 8) +
  theme_pubr() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5000, 105000), ylim = c(0.05, 1.1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 50000, 100000), labels = c("$0", "$50K", "$100K"), guide = "prism_offset") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0.1, .9, 0.2), guide = "prism_offset") +
  labs(x = "GDP per capita", y = "Mental Accounting\n(Choen's d)") +

# Flag legend --------------------------------------------------------------

fit_and_save_mIncome_Others <- function(){
  path2file <- "scr/country-level-analysis/models/Others/mIncome.rds"
  
  if( file.exists(path2file) ){
    m <- readRDS(file = path2file)
  } else {
    m <- brm(
      formula = choensd ~ zIncome + (zIncome | study), 
      prior = prior_string("normal(0,2.5)", class = "b"),
      data = df %>% group_by(study) %>% mutate(zIncome=zscore(numeric_income)),
      iter = 20000, refresh = 100, cores = 4
    )
    saveRDS(m, file = path2file)
  }
  return(m)
}
mIncome <- fit_and_save_mIncome_Others()

# Built from the already-loaded all-predictors model (mAll); mirrors the
# "All predictors" block in scr/tables.R
log10_bf_z <- function(model, var){
  pp <- prepare_predictions(model)
  posterior <- as.vector(unlist(pp$dpars$mu$fe$b[, str_c("b_z", var)]))
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(posterior), mean = 0, sd = 1)
  round(log10(as.numeric(
    bayesfactor_parameters(posterior, prior, direction = "two-sided", null = 0)
  )), 2)
}

fe <- fixef(mAll)[c("zFinancialLiteracy", "zEducation", "zAge", "zIncome"), ]

data.frame(
  ` ` = c("Financial Literacy", "Education", "Age", "Income"),
  `Standardized Estimate` = round(fe[, "Estimate"], 2),
  `95% CIs` = sprintf("%.2f, %.2f", fe[, "Q2.5"], fe[, "Q97.5"]),
  `log₁₀(BF)` = c(
    log10_bf_z(mAll, "FinancialLiteracy"),
    log10_bf_z(mAll, "Education"),
    log10_bf_z(mAll, "Age"),
    log10_bf_z(mAll, "Income")
  ),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
) %>%
  kbl(caption = "<b>Table 4 | </b> Associations of Financial Literacy and Demographic Variables with Mental Accounting",
      format = "html", row.names = FALSE, table.attr = "style='width:60%;'") %>%
  kable_classic(html_font = "Cambria") %>%

Fit Non-Linear Model 
#
d <- df %>%
  mutate(
    x = zscore(GDPxCapita),
    y = choensd,
    zdemocracy = zscore(democracy_index),
    zface_value = zscore(log(Rate_to_USD)),
    zgini = zscore(Gini)
  ) %>%
  filter(family != "binomial1")

# Define the nonlinear formula with random effects plus linear face value effect
nlform <- bf(
  y ~ K / (1 + exp(-r * (x - x0))) + betademocracy * zdemocracy + betaface * zface_value + betagini * zgini,
  K ~ 1 + (1|study),
  r ~ 1 + (1|study),
  x0 ~ 1 + (1|study),
  betademocracy ~ 1 + (1|study),
  betaface ~ 1 + (1|study),
  betagini ~ 1 + (1|study),
  nl = TRUE
)

# Define priors
priors <- c(
  prior(normal(1, 1), nlpar = "K"),
  prior(normal(0, 2.5), nlpar = "r"),
  prior(normal(-1, 1), nlpar = "x0"),
  prior(normal(0, 2.5), nlpar = "betademocracy"),
  prior(normal(0, 2.5), nlpar = "betaface"),
  prior(normal(0, 2.5), nlpar = "betagini")
)

# Fit the model
bm2 <- brm(
  formula = nlform,
  data = d,
  prior = priors,
  family = gaussian(),
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  chains = 4,
  iter = 20000,
  cores = 4,
  seed = 123
)

Multidimensional Scaling Analysis

Fit MDS 
# Perform MDS on the correlation matrix
lor2smd = sqrt( 3 / (pi^2) )
df <- theta[,c("Country", "theta", "study", "family")] %>% 
  group_by(study) %>% 
  mutate( theta = ifelse(family=="binomial", theta*lor2smd, theta)) %>% 
  na.omit() %>% ungroup() %>% 
  group_by(Country, study) %>% 
  mutate(theta=mean(theta)) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(Country, study, theta) %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = study,
    values_from = theta,
    id_cols = Country
  )

dist_matrix <- dist(t(scale(df[,-1])))
mds_fit <- cmdscale(dist_matrix, k = 3, eig = TRUE)

mds_df <- data.frame(
  x = mds_fit$points[,1],
  y = mds_fit$points[,2],
  z = mds_fit$points[,3],
  scenario = colnames(df)[-1]
)
Plot MDS

        type = "scatter3d",

df_plot <- function(m, x, study_name){
  fe <- fixef(m) %>% as.data.frame()
  fe <- data.frame(beta=fe[,1], lower=fe[,3], upper=fe[,4], var=row.names(fe))
  
  # Bayes Factor
  draws_model <- as_draws(m)
  nm <- names(draws_model[[1]])[1:nrow(fe)]
  vars <- nm[ str_detect(nm, ":") ]
  # Age
  post_age <- lapply( 1:2, function(chain) draws_model[[chain]][vars[1]] ) %>% 
    unlist() %>% as.numeric() * sd(data$Age) 
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(post_age),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf_age <- bayesfactor_parameters(post_age,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  log10_bf_age <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf_age)), 2)
  
  # Education
  post_education <- lapply( 1:2, function(chain) draws_model[[chain]][vars[2]] ) %>% 
    unlist() %>% as.numeric() * sd(data$Education)
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(post_education),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf_education <- bayesfactor_parameters(post_education,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  log10_bf_education <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf_education)), 2)
  
  # Financial Literacy
  post_fintil <- lapply( 1:2, function(chain) draws_model[[chain]][vars[3]] ) %>% 
    unlist() %>% as.numeric() * sd(data$FinancialLiteracy)
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(post_fintil),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf_fintil <- bayesfactor_parameters(post_fintil,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  log10_bf_fintil <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf_fintil)), 2)
  
  # Gender
  post_gender <- lapply( 1:2, function(chain) draws_model[[chain]][vars[4]] ) %>% 
    unlist() %>% as.numeric()
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(post_gender),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf_gender <- bayesfactor_parameters(post_gender,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  log10_bf_gender <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf_gender)), 2)
  
  # Income
  post_income <- lapply( 1:2, function(chain) draws_model[[chain]][vars[5]] ) %>% 
    unlist() %>% as.numeric() * sd(data$numeric_income, na.rm = T)
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(post_income),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf_income <- bayesfactor_parameters(post_income,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  log10_bf_income <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf_income)), 2)
  
  log10_bf <- c(log10_bf_age, log10_bf_education, log10_bf_fintil, log10_bf_gender, log10_bf_income)
  fe %>% 
    filter(stri_detect_fixed(var, ":")) %>% 
    mutate(var=sapply(str_split(var, ":"), function(x) x[2])) %>% 
    mutate(
      x=seq(x-0.2, x+0.2, length=5), 
      study=study_name,
      var=ifelse(var=="FinancialLiteracy", "Financial\nLiteracy",var),
      var=ifelse(var=="GenderMale", "Gender",var),
      var=ifelse(var=="numeric_income", "Income",var),
      `log₁₀(BF)` = log10_bf
      
    ) %>% 
    mutate(is_sign=ifelse(sign(lower)==sign(upper),"yes", "no"))
  
}

df_plot_MrAB <- function(m, x, study_name){
  fe <- fixef(m) %>% as.data.frame()
  fe <- data.frame(beta=fe[,1], lower=fe[,3], upper=fe[,4], var=row.names(fe))
  
  # Bayes Factor
  draws_model <- as_draws(m)
  nm <- names(draws_model[[1]])[1:nrow(fe)]
  vars <- nm[ 2:6 ]
  
  # Age
  post_age <- lapply( 1:2, function(chain) draws_model[[chain]][vars[1]] ) %>% 
    unlist() %>% as.numeric()
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(post_age),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf_age <- bayesfactor_parameters(post_age,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  log10_bf_age <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf_age)), 2)
  
  # Education
  post_education <- lapply( 1:2, function(chain) draws_model[[chain]][vars[2]] ) %>% 
    unlist() %>% as.numeric()
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(post_education),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf_education <- bayesfactor_parameters(post_education,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  log10_bf_education <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf_education)), 2)
  
  # Financial Literacy
  post_fintil <- lapply( 1:2, function(chain) draws_model[[chain]][vars[3]] ) %>% 
    unlist() %>% as.numeric()
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(post_fintil),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf_fintil <- bayesfactor_parameters(post_fintil,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  log10_bf_fintil <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf_fintil)), 2)
  
  # Gender
  post_gender <- lapply( 1:2, function(chain) draws_model[[chain]][vars[4]] ) %>% 
    unlist() %>% as.numeric()
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(post_gender),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf_gender <- bayesfactor_parameters(post_gender,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  log10_bf_gender <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf_gender)), 2)
  
  # Income
  post_income <- lapply( 1:2, function(chain) draws_model[[chain]][vars[5]] ) %>% 
    unlist() %>% as.numeric()
  prior <- distribution_normal(length(post_income),mean=0,sd=1)
  bf_income <- bayesfactor_parameters(post_income,prior,direction="two-sided",null=0)
  log10_bf_income <- round(log10(as.numeric(bf_income)), 2)
  
  log10_bf <- c(log10_bf_age, log10_bf_education, log10_bf_fintil, log10_bf_gender, log10_bf_income)
  fe[2:6,] %>% 
    mutate(
      x=seq(x-0.2, x+0.2, length=5), 
      study=study_name,
      var=ifelse(var=="FinancialLiteracy", "Financial\nLiteracy",var),
      var=ifelse(var=="GenderMale", "Gender",var),
      var=ifelse(var=="numeric_income", "Income",var),
      `log₁₀(BF)` = log10_bf
    ) %>% 
    mutate(is_sign=ifelse(sign(lower)==sign(upper),"yes", "no"))
  
}

  mutate(x = x+rep(c(0.2, 0.1, 0, -0.1, -0.2), 8))

Individual- and Country-level Correlations

Figure 3 as reported in the manuscript. Across all panels, the MrAB gain and loss measures are averaged into a single MrAB index, so that each of the seven scenarios is represented by one measure. The code that computes each panel is shown in the (folded) chunks below.

Setup: variables, palette, helpers 
library(psych)        # mixed (tetrachoric/polyserial) correlations
library(metafor)      # meta-analysis of correlations
library(lme4)         # mixed-effects models
library(performance)  # R2 (Nakagawa / Tjur)
library(relaimpo)     # LMG variance decomposition
library(corrplot)

# Earlier sections load packages (e.g., MASS) that mask dplyr verbs; re-bind them
select <- dplyr::select
filter <- dplyr::filter

binary_vars     <- c("MrAB1", "MrAB2", "Jacket", "Play", "Plane")
continuous_vars <- c("Game", "Drink", "Gym")
all_vars        <- c("MrAB1", "MrAB2", "Game", "Drink", "Jacket", "Play", "Gym", "Plane")
scenario_labels <- c("MrAB", "Game", "Drink", "Jacket", "Play", "Gym", "Plane")
scenario_colors <- colorspace::qualitative_hcl(7, "Dark 3")[c(5, 2, 4, 7, 6, 1, 3)]
names(scenario_colors) <- c("MrAB", "Game", "Play", "Drink", "Jacket", "Plane", "Gym")
corr_palette    <- colorRampPalette(c("#053061", "white", "#67001F"))(200)

# Add correlation values + significance stars onto a (lower-triangle) corrplot
add_corrplot_text <- function(r_mat, p_mat, cex = 1.0) {
  n <- nrow(r_mat)
  for (i in 2:n) for (j in 1:(i - 1)) {
    stars <- ""
    if (!is.na(p_mat[i, j])) {
      if (p_mat[i, j] < 0.001) stars <- "***"
      else if (p_mat[i, j] < 0.01) stars <- "**"
      else if (p_mat[i, j] < 0.05) stars <- "*"
    }
    text(j, n - i + 1, paste0(sprintf("%.2f", r_mat[i, j]), stars), cex = cex)
  }
}

Left: meta-analyzed individual-level correlation matrix across the seven scenarios. Right: partial R² decomposition (variance explained when predicting each scenario from the others). The two MrAB conditions are averaged into a single MrAB index.

Within-country mixed correlations + meta-analysis 
# Tetrachoric (binary-binary), polyserial (binary-continuous), Pearson (cont-cont)
safe_tetrachoric <- function(x, y) tryCatch({
  if (length(unique(x)) < 2 || length(unique(y)) < 2) return(NA)
  tetrachoric(cbind(x, y), correct = 0.5)$rho[1, 2]
}, error = function(e) NA)
safe_polyserial <- function(b, c) tryCatch({
  if (length(unique(b)) < 2 || sd(c, na.rm = TRUE) == 0 ||
      sum(!is.na(b) & !is.na(c)) < 10) return(NA)
  r <- as.numeric(polyserial(c, b))
  if (is.na(r) || abs(r) > 1) r <- cor(as.numeric(b), c, use = "complete.obs")
  r
}, error = function(e) tryCatch(cor(as.numeric(b), c, use = "complete.obs"),
                                error = function(e2) NA))

# Standardize continuous indicators within country, then per-country correlation matrix
df_standardized <- df_indicators %>% group_by(Country) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(continuous_vars), ~ as.vector(scale(.)))) %>% ungroup()

compute_country_correlation <- function(data) {
  mat <- na.omit(as.data.frame(data[, all_vars]))
  if (nrow(mat) < 30) return(NULL)
  n <- length(all_vars)
  cm <- matrix(NA, n, n, dimnames = list(all_vars, all_vars)); diag(cm) <- 1
  for (i in 1:(n - 1)) for (j in (i + 1):n) {
    x <- mat[[all_vars[i]]]; y <- mat[[all_vars[j]]]
    ib <- all_vars[i] %in% binary_vars; jb <- all_vars[j] %in% binary_vars
    r <- if (ib && jb) safe_tetrachoric(x, y)
         else if (ib && !jb) safe_polyserial(x, y)
         else if (!ib && jb) safe_polyserial(y, x)
         else cor(x, y, use = "complete.obs")
    cm[i, j] <- r; cm[j, i] <- r
  }
  list(cor_matrix = cm, n = nrow(mat))
}
country_results <- lapply(split(df_standardized, df_standardized$Country), compute_country_correlation)
Within-country mixed correlations + meta-analysis 
country_results <- country_results[!sapply(country_results, is.null)]

# Fisher-z random-effects meta-analysis of each pair, back-transformed
meta_pvalues <- do.call(rbind, lapply(combn(all_vars, 2, simplify = FALSE), function(pair) {
  cors <- sapply(country_results, function(x) x$cor_matrix[pair[1], pair[2]])
  ns   <- sapply(country_results, function(x) x$n)
  ok <- !is.na(cors); cors <- cors[ok]; ns <- ns[ok]
  if (length(cors) < 3) return(data.frame(var1 = pair[1], var2 = pair[2], r_pooled = NA, p_value = NA))
  fit <- tryCatch(rma(yi = atanh(cors), vi = 1 / (ns - 3), method = "REML"), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(data.frame(var1 = pair[1], var2 = pair[2], r_pooled = NA, p_value = NA))
  data.frame(var1 = pair[1], var2 = pair[2], r_pooled = tanh(as.numeric(fit$beta)), p_value = fit$pval)
}))

# Combine MrAB1 & MrAB2 into a single 7x7 matrix (average r, max/conservative p)
get_pair <- function(d, a, b, col) d[[col]][(d$var1 == a & d$var2 == b) | (d$var1 == b & d$var2 == a)]
individual_r <- matrix(NA, 7, 7, dimnames = list(scenario_labels, scenario_labels)); diag(individual_r) <- 1
individual_p <- matrix(NA, 7, 7, dimnames = list(scenario_labels, scenario_labels)); diag(individual_p) <- 0
others <- setdiff(scenario_labels, "MrAB")
for (v in others) {
  r1 <- get_pair(meta_pvalues, "MrAB1", v, "r_pooled"); r2 <- get_pair(meta_pvalues, "MrAB2", v, "r_pooled")
  p1 <- get_pair(meta_pvalues, "MrAB1", v, "p_value");  p2 <- get_pair(meta_pvalues, "MrAB2", v, "p_value")
  individual_r["MrAB", v] <- individual_r[v, "MrAB"] <- mean(c(r1, r2), na.rm = TRUE)
  individual_p["MrAB", v] <- individual_p[v, "MrAB"] <- max(c(p1, p2), na.rm = TRUE)
}
for (i in seq_along(others)) for (j in seq_along(others)) if (i < j) {
  rv <- get_pair(meta_pvalues, others[i], others[j], "r_pooled")
  pv <- get_pair(meta_pvalues, others[i], others[j], "p_value")
  if (length(rv) && !is.na(rv[1])) {
    individual_r[others[i], others[j]] <- individual_r[others[j], others[i]] <- rv[1]
    individual_p[others[i], others[j]] <- individual_p[others[j], others[i]] <- pv[1]
  }
}

Individual-level variance explained (drop-one ΔR²) 
df_scaled <- df_indicators %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(continuous_vars), ~ scale(.)[, 1], .names = "{.col}_z"))
get_r2 <- function(m, is_binary) if (is_binary)
  tryCatch(as.numeric(r2_tjur(m)), error = function(e) NA_real_) else
  tryCatch(as.numeric(r2_nakagawa(m)$R2_marginal), error = function(e) NA_real_)

individual_partial_r2 <- data.frame()
for (target in all_vars) {
  is_binary <- target %in% binary_vars
  preds <- setdiff(all_vars, target)
  pnames <- sapply(preds, function(p) if (p %in% continuous_vars) paste0(p, "_z") else p)
  if (!is_binary) { df_scaled[[paste0(target, "_z")]] <- scale(df_scaled[[target]])[, 1]; tvar <- paste0(target, "_z") } else tvar <- target
  fit <- function(fm) if (is_binary)
    glmer(fm, df_scaled, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))) else
    lmer(fm, df_scaled, REML = FALSE)
  full <- fit(as.formula(paste(tvar, "~", paste(pnames, collapse = " + "), "+ (1|Country)")))
  r2_full <- get_r2(full, is_binary)
  delta <- setNames(numeric(length(preds)), preds)
  for (i in seq_along(preds)) {
    red <- fit(as.formula(paste(tvar, "~", paste(pnames[-i], collapse = " + "), "+ (1|Country)")))
    delta[preds[i]] <- max(r2_full - get_r2(red, is_binary), 0)
  }
  pr2 <- if (sum(delta) > 0) (delta / sum(delta)) * r2_full else delta
  individual_partial_r2 <- rbind(individual_partial_r2,
    data.frame(target = target, predictor = preds, partial_r2 = pr2, r2_total = r2_full))
}

# Combine MrAB1/MrAB2 (sum as predictors; average the two MrAB targets)
mrab_t <- individual_partial_r2 %>% filter(target %in% c("MrAB1", "MrAB2")) %>%
  mutate(predictor = ifelse(predictor %in% c("MrAB1", "MrAB2"), "MrAB", predictor)) %>%
  group_by(target, predictor) %>% summarise(partial_r2 = sum(partial_r2), r2_total = first(r2_total), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(predictor) %>% summarise(partial_r2 = mean(partial_r2), r2_total = mean(r2_total), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(target = "MrAB") %>% filter(predictor != "MrAB")
other_t <- individual_partial_r2 %>% filter(!target %in% c("MrAB1", "MrAB2")) %>%
  mutate(predictor = ifelse(predictor %in% c("MrAB1", "MrAB2"), "MrAB", predictor)) %>%
  group_by(target, predictor) %>% summarise(partial_r2 = sum(partial_r2), r2_total = first(r2_total), .groups = "drop")
individual_combined <- bind_rows(mrab_t, other_t)
Plot: individual-level variance explained 
individual_combined %>%
  mutate(partial_r2_pct = partial_r2 * 100,
         target = factor(target, levels = rev(scenario_labels)),
         predictor = factor(predictor, levels = scenario_labels)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(target, partial_r2_pct, fill = predictor)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = scenario_colors, name = "Predictor") +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-.1, 85)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Variance Explained (%)") +
  theme_pubr(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.7, 0.7), text = element_text(size = 15))

Left: country-level correlation matrix (Pearson correlations of country effect sizes). Right: partial R² decomposition (LMG method). The two MrAB conditions are averaged into a single MrAB index.

Country effect-size matrix, correlations, and LMG 
# Country x scenario effect-size matrix (binomial log-ORs mapped to SMD; MrAB averaged)
lor2smd <- sqrt(3 / (pi^2))
df_country <- map_dfr(theta_preregisteredExclusion, ~ .x)[, c("Country", "theta", "study", "family")] %>%
  group_by(study) %>% mutate(theta = ifelse(family == "binomial", theta * lor2smd, theta)) %>%
  na.omit() %>% ungroup() %>%
  group_by(Country, study) %>% summarise(theta = mean(theta), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = study, values_from = theta, id_cols = Country)

# Country-level correlation matrix + p-values
country_r <- matrix(NA, 7, 7, dimnames = list(scenario_labels, scenario_labels)); diag(country_r) <- 1
country_p <- matrix(NA, 7, 7, dimnames = list(scenario_labels, scenario_labels)); diag(country_p) <- 0
for (i in seq_along(scenario_labels)) for (j in seq_along(scenario_labels)) if (i < j) {
  ct <- cor.test(df_country[[scenario_labels[i]]], df_country[[scenario_labels[j]]])
  country_r[i, j] <- country_r[j, i] <- ct$estimate
  country_p[i, j] <- country_p[j, i] <- ct$p.value
}

# Country-level LMG variance decomposition (lm per scenario, relaimpo)
country_partial_r2 <- data.frame()
for (target in scenario_labels) {
  preds <- setdiff(scenario_labels, target)
  m <- lm(as.formula(paste0("`", target, "` ~ ", paste0("`", preds, "`", collapse = " + "))), data = df_country)
  lmg <- calc.relimp(m, type = "lmg")@lmg
  country_partial_r2 <- rbind(country_partial_r2, data.frame(
    target = target, predictor = gsub("`", "", names(lmg)),
    partial_r2 = as.numeric(lmg), r2_total = summary(m)$r.squared))
}
Plot: country-level correlation matrix 
corrplot(country_r, method = "color", diag = FALSE, type = "lower",
         col.lim = c(-1, 1), col = corr_palette, tl.col = "black",
         tl.cex = 1.4, tl.srt = 45, tl.offset = 0.8, mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
add_corrplot_text(country_r, country_p)
Plot: country-level variance explained 
country_partial_r2 %>%
  mutate(partial_r2_pct = partial_r2 * 100,
         target = factor(target, levels = rev(scenario_labels)),
         predictor = factor(predictor, levels = scenario_labels)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(target, partial_r2_pct, fill = predictor)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = scenario_colors, name = "Predictor") +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-.1, 85)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Variance Explained (%)") +
  theme_pubr(base_size = 12) +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15), legend.position = "none")
